title: Jacobi exceptional orthogonal polynomials for extended Scarf I potentials with position-dependent mass
abstract: We show that the Scarf I potential problem in a position-dependent mass background of the type $m(α;x) = (1 + α\sin x)^{-2}$, $0<α<1$, can be solved by using a point canonical transformation mapping the corresponding Schr\" odinger equation onto that of the Scarf I potential with constant mass. The inverse point canonical transformation then provides some exactly-solvable rational extensions of the Scarf I potential with positive-dependent mass associated with $X_m$-Jacobi exceptional orthogonal polynomials of type I, II, or III. The Scarf I potential problem with position-dependent mass is shown to exhibit a deformed shape invariance property in a deformed supersymmetric framework. Such a property is also valid for extended potentials of type I and II. The results are illustrated with a simple example.
summary: This paper tackles the complex problem of finding exact solutions for a Schrödinger equation featuring both a Scarf I potential and a position-dependent mass. It achieves this by employing Point Canonical Transformations to simplify the Hamiltonian, revealing that the system possesses deformed shape invariance. The results characterize the energy spectrum using specialized mathematical tools like $X_m$-Jacobi exceptional orthogonal polynomials.
main_problem: The research aims to find exactly-solvable rational extensions of the Scarf I potential that incorporate a position-dependent mass (PDM) background.
main_result: The PDM Scarf I potential exhibits deformed shape invariance, and its solutions are characterized by $X_m$-Jacobi exceptional orthogonal polynomials (EOPs).
method: The core methodology involves using Point Canonical Transformations (PCT) to map the complex PDM Schrödinger equation onto a simpler constant-mass system, followed by analyzing the resulting structure using deformed supersymmetric quantum mechanics.
